statement: The random forest's standard settings — 500 trees, each on a bootstrap of every row, mtry floor(p/3) for a class outcome and floor(√p) for a numeric outcome — are randomForest's and ranger's documented defaults.

Under-reporting of energy is systematic and concentrated among people with higher BMI and weight-conscious participants, so excluding under-reporters when the outcome is adiposity removes a non-random slice of the studied population, which is why many analyses keep everyone.
regime: dietary lens; intake screens; adiposity-related outcomes
decision: the exclusions card's why, term and drawer

statement: Complementary-pairs stability selection with B = 50 pairs of random halves, each half's first q variables on the lasso path, threshold tau = 0.6 and q = floor((2*tau - 1)*p) keeps the expected number of falsely selected predictors at or below 1, by Meinshausen & Bühlmann's bound q^2/((2*tau - 1)p), which complementary pairs keep under the same exchangeability assumption.
regime: prediction with many candidate predictors (p in the tens to thousands), any outcome
claimed_basis: variable_selection.py:57-59; Meinshausen & Bühlmann 2010 Thm 1; Shah & Samworth 2013 (JRSS B 75:55); tau at the lower end of (0.6, 0.9).

statement: Under the partition energy model with an addition contrast, the counterfactual 'one unit more of the exposure' must also raise total energy by the exposure's kcal per unit, so that energy from the other sources stays fixed, because the partition model derives other-source energy from the total.
regime: inference; binary outcome; marginal measure; energy-bearing exposure; addition contrast; partition model
decision: how the high setting is built for g-computation

statement: Absolute risks cannot be predicted from individually matched case-control sets, as a limit of the design: the conditional likelihood removes every set's intercept so there is no baseline risk to recalibrate, and matched controls are not a random sample of non-cases, so no single offset turns the sample's odds into anyone's risk.

For an observed risk ratio RR above 1, the E-value is RR + √(RR − 1), so a risk ratio of 2 has an E-value of 3: an unmeasured confounder would need risk ratios of 3 with both exposure and outcome to explain it away.
regime: sensitivity to unmeasured confounding for a risk ratio above 1

statement: Under prediction, Riley's minimum sample size should count as candidate predictor parameters one per numeric predictor, k - 1 per category of k levels, every column a declared spline or quintile form adds, and k - 2 extra columns for every bendable continuous predictor when Explore's spline rule (or inner-CV choice) is on, with k by Harrell's rule on the effective size; events are the rarer class's count for a yes/no outcome (smallest class for several classes), counted on the training rows only; under inference every analyzed row is counted.
regime: prediction (shelf before families are chosen); inference counts all analyzed rows
decision: Riley's minimum and the shelf order (regression families first below it)
claimed_basis: Riley et al., BMJ 2020;368:m441 ('candidate predictor parameters' count non-linear terms); WP8; EXPLORE repair.

statement: On a food-frequency questionnaire a blank frequently means 'never', especially among older participants, so that missingness is not at random, and standard multiple imputation, which assumes it is, is an improvement but not a solution.

For a time-to-event outcome under prediction with no declared prediction horizon, scoring predicted risk (Brier score and calibration) at the median follow-up time of the training rows is an appropriate default horizon.
regime: Time-to-event outcome; prediction; no prediction horizon declared
decision: Horizon at which risk predictions are scored and calibrated
claimed_basis: METHODS_REFERENCE contract horizon_calibration: 'stated: the prediction horizon is declared with the follow-up, else the median follow-up time'

statement: Under inference, a site that differs in both the exposure and the outcome confounds the estimate and intervals that treat its participants as independent are too narrow, so each site gets its own intercept and cluster-robust intervals (few groups needing a small-sample correction), 'cluster only' leaves between-group differences in the estimate, and under prediction validation keeps a group together.
regime: participants grouped in sites, households or batches
claimed_basis: none stated (the drawer cites NUTRITION_PACK §08 for split hygiene)

statement: Multiple imputation with the outcome in the imputation model is invalid under prediction, because a held-out row's own outcome would fill its predictors and a new row has none; under prediction blanks must be filled in each training fold without the outcome.
regime: prediction, missing predictor values, strategy = multiple_imputation
decision: refusal of multiple imputation under prediction, with in-fold fill and complete cases as exits
claimed_basis: Sisk et al. 2023; BLUEPRINT §12 ruling 4; audit WP7, ME-01.

statement: Under a population survey design, a subgroup analysis keeps every row and marks the domain, since deleting rows drops PSUs and strata from the variance and gives wrong standard errors; variances are Taylor-linearized with first-stage units sampled with replacement and t intervals on the PSUs minus the strata holding the domain's rows.
regime: survey design with weights, strata and PSUs; exclusions or complete cases under the population answer
